::: {#rem-confidence-interval-exact}
#### Exact and conservative intervals

@def-confidence-interval requires the [confidence coefficient](#def-confidence-coefficient)
to be at least $1 - \siglevel$.
The coverage probability can depend on $\param$,
and the confidence coefficient is its smallest value.
An interval is exact when its coverage probability equals $1 - \siglevel$
for every $\param$,
and conservative when its coverage probability is larger than $1 - \siglevel$
for some $\param$.
Discrete data usually allow only a conservative interval.
A region that need not be an interval is a confidence set
[@CaseBerg01, Section 9.1].
:::
